notes: Coverall's Item 19 is non-standard. Rather than disclosing revenue, profit, or sales metrics, it discloses operational fulfillment data about how many of the 329 franchise packages sold in fiscal year 2025 were filled within the contractually required time period, broken down by package size tier ($3000, $4000, $5000, $7000, $10000). The 'package size' appears to represent the dollar value of initial business (cleaning contracts) the franchisor commits to provide. The disclosure covers: (a) packages filled on time, (b) fulfillment period not yet expired, (c) franchisees who accepted performance, (d) packages adjusted, and (e) disputed packages. The document explicitly states 'Other than the preceding financial performance representation, we do not make any representations about a franchised business's future financial performance or the past financial performance of company-owned or franchised outlets.' This is a limited and atypical Item 19 disclosure. No revenue, profit, or traditional financial metrics are disclosed. The records above capture the fulfillment count data that constitutes the FPR; downstream breakeven calculations should not be applied to these records.
